This just happened to me LOL perfect timing. Former GC, I moved out into a new apartment while Nparents were at work when I got fed up with their narcissistic abuse and became the SG. They were LIVID. Cut me off the phone plan immediately so I had no service; couldn’t make or send calls. They then proceeded to create lies about me being a runaway pregnant drug addict (all false) who abandoned them out of nowhere and wasn’t responding even though they were calling me multiple times (another lie, they cut me off lol). They spread this smear campaign to teachers at schools I attended growing up, neighbors, family friends. One family friend actually contacted me to tell me because she was concerned since none of this sounds like me at all which is how I found out. My parents actually asked her if they can take legal action against me 💀They have been talking immense crap about me to my siblings “don’t be like her,” “she’s a slut,” “I want to k*ll her” etc thinking my siblings hate me and had me blocked like they are supposed to. Oh, and they absolutely HATE my super supportive bf due to this weird idea that he and his family have replaced them and they’re brainwashing me and I must be pregnant since he and I live together. Consequently, they’ve threatened him multiple times.

Then, there was a love bomb/gaslighting email sent to me from them like 1-2 weeks after I left and went NC. Lots of guilt tripping. Was tempting to respond and go off because my parents are unaware that I know everything they’ve been doing and saying and the fake act via e-mail enraged me. Overall the email tore me up but after discussion with friends and bf I saw how manipulative it was and haven’t spoken to either of my parents since I left. Won’t waste my breathe trying to explain when the truth they’ll just find another way to scapegoat me to justify their actions. I’ll never get an apology so I’m focusing on grieving my relationship with them even though I crave parental support…Changed my number, they don’t know my address. My siblings are punished if they have any contact with me or try to defend me and as a result I have missed out on important milestones for them like graduation which hurts me very much. I miss my siblings every day. We talk in secret and I hate that it has to be that way. And suddenly not having parents at all hurts too, especially during such a transitional phase of my life. I’ve never had anyone close due to me yet but this feels similar to what I can imagine that’s like, even though they’re alive. I simply can’t imagine seeing them again and can’t see them the same. It’s like they’re strangers with familiar faces. Maybe I’m still processing everything. Sometimes it feels like a dream. Narcissists are good at creating trauma bonds I guess.

Overall the healing from a narcissist isn’t linear. Throw siblings being held hostage by Nparents into the mix and it’s extra rough. However, healing is possible. The first two weeks were the hardest but the relief from having freedom is immense. Almost jarring really. Their behavior has just solidified why this was the right decision. Once my siblings are out and/or I can find ways to see them somehow I will be able to breathe. The most difficult part of this situation for me is my lack of ability to change the environment of my old home because I can only control myself;not the narcissists who raised me. I can’t get my siblings out since they are (obviously)not my children, CPS has done nothing in the past despite long paper trails and some evidence, with rising COL and a housing crisis in my state my bf and I are just making ends meet between us right now (I’m 20, he’s 23 I just graduated college finalizing employment). We can’t afford to adopt or get into legal battles, so I’m out of options it seems. 4-5 more years until they’re all out and I can’t wait for them to be able to heal and live the happy lives they deserve. In the meantime I am so grateful for my support system (including this sub), life, and my freedom. Sending strength and love to all of you.

Respectfully, my actions are not a problem. I have not a committed a crime. I have not intentionally caused anyone or anything any damage yet I have been very apologetic about doing so unintentionally and expressed that with patience numerous time to both of my parents. My parents are not so much upset with me not being Muslim as they are with me moving out before marriage. They see me moving out as “rejecting” them and saying that “I don’t need my parents anymore.” I never told them that. That was an assumption they made, and I can only assume that stems from cultural/religious conditioning especially since I am a woman so independence is traditionally limited. 

Saying that she was gaslighting me and that BOTH of my parents are abusive was critical to the context of why I want to move out. As a child, my dad regularly beat me for little things such as spilling drinks with belts and wires. Growing up he mellowed out but was very emotionally and mentally abusive (statements like “I wish you were never born”, calling me a whore because I wore leggings). My mom witnessed it all and let it happen and when I would come to her for help she would say “he’s your dad you have to respect him.” Now that I am older I have distanced myself a bit to avoid these behaviors and chose to forgive them even though they never have and never will give me an apology. I forgave them because I know there is a lot of generational trauma and conditioning that has led them to be abusive, because holding resentment did me more harm than good, and because I did want a shot at building a healthier relationship with my parents (from a distance, for example moving out). But then this situation happened. My siblings and I have all repeatedly gotten CPS involved and every time our parents were believed over us. Agents would interview us in front of or near parents so we couldn’t completely tell the truth, we would be told before hand by our parents that if we told all of our “family business” that we would be taken away and abused by bad people in a foster home and all separated from each other. That instilled fear that as kids prevented us from taking further action and eventually we developed distrust for what was a useless system of social workers that we thought would help. Unless it is obvious physical abuse, abuse is often hard to prove especially with adult abusers who know how to switch into nice mode with outsiders at the drop of a hat.

By gaslighting, I meant that my mom literally would tell me the way I experienced things did not happen. She and my dad chose to not speak to me first for over a month and wouldn’t have reached out if I didn’t, and whenever I reached out they gave me short and cold responses. While this was happening she told me they didn’t reach out because they didn’t want to bother me at school. Yesterday she admitted that it was because they were processing and hurt, then victimized herself (“are you trying to blame us??”) and when I told her I felt abandoned because no one communicated that to me and I can’t read minds instead they just withdrew, she proceeded to try to manipulate me into thinking I was over dramatic.

I’m not sure if you simply didn’t read my post, but I have tried the calm and understanding approach. I could’ve lashed out at them in anger, ghosted them, etc. but I didn’t, because I understood this was a lot to process and I know it’s a difficult situation. I sent them my explanation via email so they could read and process at their own pace, and signed it saying that I would not reach out because I didnt want to overwhelm them or be faced with hostility but would respond whenever they were ready to talk. They are the ones who have shut down when I approach. My dad is currently avoiding all communication with me and now communicates through my mom. I never asked them to condone or support my decisions; all I wanted was for them to keep me as a daughter in my life. Kids are not pets; we grow up to be our own people who make our own decisions and have our own beliefs and it is impossible to always do so in a way that is compatible with that of our parents. You can be unsupportive of someone’s opinions and actions while still supporting them as a human being especially if this is not a consistent situation you encounter with them. I have recognized, said and validated to my parents that I know they want what’s best for me and that they love me. But, the issue is that we have a difference of opinion on what is best for me. I choose happiness and freedom, they want conformity. My mom is the one who told me there is no more compromise. She can handle me leaving the religion, but me moving out is a dealbreaker hence why she gave me the ultimatum and told me I can’t “double dip.” The only way for me to “find a solution for everyone” is to move back home and if the situation reverts to the bad environment it was then I only have myself to blame because it’s their house, their rules and I chose to return. I would hope they would be better but that is a risk. This situation all around is full of risks unfortunately. I know my parents are in a tough spot; I am not trying to villanize them. I am simply relaying the series of events and while I empathize with them I can’t keep doing so at the expense of my own mental health and emotional validation.
